items.title: privacy page: a line about visit counts
items.text_label: proposed line (html, as it would go in content.py)
items.text: • visit counts: we count requests to the site by day, the kind of page, the site that linked here and the country. no IP address, no account and no cookie go with them. we use them to see whether shwarm is working for people.
items.note: Proposed for the "what we collect" list on the privacy page (scripts/pages/content.py). The privacy page also still says to email support@ to download your data or close your account; both are now buttons in the account modal, so that line could change to point there.

items.title: manifesto and holding page still talk about lobbies
items.text: docs/manifesto.md and mockups/holding.html (the live shwarm.org holding page) still say things like 'the same seat in a lobby', 'joining is the vote: a new shwarm opens when enough people join its lobby' and 'a new shwarm opens a lobby and starts when enough people join'. Go-live 8.1 says Myra words these lines.
items.note: Myra: write the new lines here (or say "you draft it"), and Claude updates the manifesto and the holding page.

items.title: launch list still has lobby sizes and a variant
items.text: docs/launch-shwarms.json has 'lobby': 2 on every entry (the import ignores it now) and the survival entry's text says 'this variant of minecraft in doom'.
items.note: OK for Claude to drop the lobby fields and reword the survival entry as building on minecraft in doom?

items.title: project instructions (CLAUDE.md): proposed updates
items.text: Add to 'Never reintroduce': (1) a lobby of any kind: lobby size, seats, kickoff, the filling tab, the lobby score, join as a gate (now: a shwarm is live the moment it is posted; join says 'I'm working on it'); (2) variants: 'start a variant', ?variant=, variant_of, a variants box (now: a different finish line is a new shwarm; continuing an ended one is build on); (3) reopening: a repro that reopens a pass, the author reopening a dead end, "it's broken? post a repro" (now: an ended shwarm is locked; build on continues or challenges it). And in the folder map, new.html: '?builds_on=<path>' replaces '?variant=<path>'.
items.note: Another session has uncommitted edits in CLAUDE.md, so Claude has not touched it. Yes = Claude makes these edits once that session is done.

items.full_text: **Re-pitch, late joiners, own-post edit and delete, "make it a branch", no "claimed by": build defaults.** proposed (builder's defaults for go-live 4.4 and 4.8, Oct 9; Myra hasn't confirmed; [open #79](open-questions.md#79-re-pitch-late-join-delete-and-make-it-a-branch-edges)). *Re-pitch* ([table B #30](go-live.md#table-b-defaults-to-build-on-accept-all-in-one-go-or-change-any-row)): while a shwarm or variant is a lobby, its author changes the title and what from their own box ("re-pitch it"), behind the password like the other author acts; the done test, checks, license and address stay. Each re-pitch keeps the version it replaces, shown newest first under "re-pitched" below the what. It counts as a thread post toward the posting pace; the same words again change nothing. The new words go through triage like a new node's (A8): a cleared lobby is seen only by its author until it's cleared again (a launch shwarm stays public while it's checked), a held one stays held for Myra, a blocked one can't be re-pitched; an answer about words replaced meanwhile is dropped. *Late joiners* (LOBBY-5): once a shwarm is live, "join" sits under its contributors, with no seat limit; a late joiner gets a seat past the lobby size (no second kickoff, no kickoff notice), shows among the contributors and on their profile as working on it, and gets the node's later notices; seats stay after kickoff, as before. Contributors on a live shwarm now list seat holders who haven't posted, after those who have. *Own posts* (go-live 4.8, table B #30): "edit" and "delete" on every plain post of your own, under the same name, as a plain act (no password); edits work as on the pinned post (supersedes "the page offers 'edit' only on the pinned post until 4.8" in the 4.6 entry). A deleted post becomes a tombstone ("this post was deleted.") with its name and time; its replies stay; its text, links, earlier versions and mentions are erased; it still counts in the thread's numbers and keeps its upvotes; a deleted pinned post unpins. A deleted post takes no edit, upvote, reply or built-on. No edit or delete API at launch. *"make it a branch"* (shwarm.html) on plain posts of a live node opens the branch form under it, its title the post's first line and its what the post's text. *"claimed by"* (table B #19, no claim state) is gone from the shwarm mockup and the site; a test keeps it out of every template.

items.full_text: **Re-pitch history shows everyone only words they could already read.** proposed (builder's default from the go-live 4.4 review, Oct 9; Myra hasn't confirmed; [open #79](open-questions.md#79-re-pitch-late-join-delete-and-make-it-a-branch-edges)). Triage reads only a node's current title and what, so an earlier version replaced while it was still being checked or held was never cleared. Each version a re-pitch replaces notes whether everyone could read it then (cleared, or a launch shwarm still being checked). Under "re-pitched", everyone sees only those; the author sees every version. Myra's triage script prints every earlier version with who sees it. Deleting the pinned post also blanks the feed card's status line at once, rather than at the next stats run; the next run fills in the fallback line.

items.full_text: **Ended shwarms are locked and nothing reopens: build defaults.** proposed (builder's defaults for go-live A11 and 5.6 under "An ended shwarm is locked", "Continuing an ended shwarm is always build on" and "A passed shwarm stays passed" (all decided Oct 9, below), Oct 9; Myra hasn't confirmed; [open #92](open-questions.md#92-locked-nodes-build-on-and-challenged-by-the-builds-edges)). Built in `apps/site`. *Reopening is gone:* no repro on a passed submission, no author's reopen of a dead end, no reopen control, form act or core command; an API body with `kind: "reopen"` is now an unknown kind (`400`), superseding that part of the site-only list in "The agent API's calls". What was recorded before stays: `reopened` audit rows, a pass on a node a repro reopened, its "reopened" pill and history line; such a pass takes no more checks. There is no reopened mail. *Locked:* a closed or dead-end node refuses posts, replies, pins, edits and deletes of posts, joins, leaves, submissions and checks in core, all with `409 shwarm_closed` and `state` (`closed` or `dead_end`) beside it ("<path> passed. it's locked: it takes nothing new", "<path> is a dead end. it's locked: …"); no code of its own for a dead end. Upvotes on its posts still count, since the decision doesn't name them. A person can't delete their own post on an ended node either; the operator's takedown stays the way to remove one. The page shows a "locked" box in place of the compose box, and no pin, join, edit, delete, "make it a branch" or author's box; the agent prompt says the same. *Build on:* `builds_on` (the create form, core and the API) takes a shwarm that passed or is a dead end, never a live one; a dead end's page shows "build on this", as a passed shwarm's does. `/new?builds_on=` naming an ended shwarm fills "done when" with its done test, to keep or change; only "done when", not its checks; nothing enforces it. *Challenged by:* the result page lists the public shwarms that build on it and kept its "done when" word for word under "challenged by", above "built on this", which lists the rest; any edit, however small, makes it building on it. The new words are in [wording to approve](copy-to-approve.md#a11-56-locked-nodes-build-on-challenged-by).

items.full_text: **A branch under an ended shwarm is locked with it.** proposed (review fix for go-live A11, Oct 9; Myra hasn't confirmed; [open #92](open-questions.md#92-locked-nodes-build-on-and-challenged-by-the-builds-edges)). Adds to "Ended shwarms are locked and nothing reopens: build defaults" below. "An ended shwarm is locked" (decided Oct 9) doesn't say what happens to the branches still live under it. Built in `apps/site` as the safe default: once a shwarm, or any branch above, passed or is a dead end, every node under it takes nothing new either: no posts, replies, pins, edits, deletes, submissions, checks, sub-branches or dead-end marks, and nothing under it can pass. Core refuses with the same `409 shwarm_closed`, naming the ended node ("<shwarm> passed. it's locked: it takes nothing new") with `state` and `locked_by` beside it. The branch's own state stays `live`, so its pill still says live. Its page shows the locked box ("<shwarm> passed, so this branch takes nothing new either. to carry it on, build on it."), with no sub-branch, "make it a branch", edit, delete or author's box; its submission page offers no check or sign-off; the branch form under it is refused; the agent prompt says "locked: <shwarm> passed, so this takes nothing new either." Upvotes still count. In the owner's inbox, a mention on an ended thread, or on one under an ended shwarm, has no reply box, only "see thread". The new words are listed in [open #92](open-questions.md#92-locked-nodes-build-on-and-challenged-by-the-builds-edges).

items.full_text: **The account modal: build defaults.** proposed (builder's defaults for go-live 6.2, Oct 9; Myra hasn't confirmed; [open #84](open-questions.md#84-the-account-modals-edges)). The modal is [the mockup's](../mockups/profile.html), on the owner's own profile only. *Without script* "account" is a link to `/@handle?account=1`, which shows the modal open, and × links back; with script it opens in place and ×, Esc and the scrim close it. *Fields:* a display name field is added (the mockup has none; go-live 6.2 and ID-4 ask for it), editable any time, up to 50 characters; the about line is one line of 160 characters; the two links are "website" and "code", http(s) only, at most 200 characters, and an address typed without `https://` gets it. *Saving* (all fields, the email and the notices together) and *change password* each ask for the password inline while the 10-minute window is closed, as the sign-off does; a mistake in the form is shown first, so the password isn't spent on it. *Email change:* the new address gets a link that lasts 24 hours and opens a page with one button; the old address is warned at once (security mail) and stays on the account, for sign-in and mail, until the button is pressed; a newer change kills the older link; confirming marks the new address verified, kills reset links sent to the old one and keeps every session. An address that already has another account gets no link, but the page and the warning are the same, so the modal never shows whether an address has an account. Throwaway domains are refused as at sign-up. The new-address mail counts toward the account mail caps (3 an hour, 10 a day per address). The beta allow-list isn't checked on a change, and founding stays. *Notices:* "new in your inbox" covers mentions (sent from 6.3) and sign-off mails, on by default, a daily digest by default (the mockup's first choice); "passes or fails" is off by default, as the mockup draws it; "a key is used somewhere new" is always on. A box shows ticked only while every type under it is on, and a save changes only the boxes that changed, so it never turns back on a type someone unsubscribed from in a mail. *Change password:* the new one twice, 10 to 128 characters, not in a breach; every other session ends, this browser stays signed in, and the "password changed" mail goes. "last changed" comes from a new column (migration 0011) and shows the joined date until the first change. *Sign out everywhere* ends every session, this browser's too, needs no password (it can only sign the person out), and lands on sign-in with "you're signed out everywhere.". Two contrast fixes to the mockup: the "✓ verified" badge sits on moss (white on leaf is 3.4:1), and the character count is a little darker. All new words wait on Myra's yes.

Adds to "The account modal: build defaults" below. *Stopping it:* a pending email change link stops working when the password is reset or changed (so the old address's warning, "if this wasn't you, reset your password", really stops a takeover), on "sign out everywhere", and when the account is saved with its own address in the email field. items.full_text: **Notice emails: build defaults.** proposed (builder's defaults for go-live 6.3 and the 4.4 kickoff mail, Oct 9; Myra hasn't confirmed; [open #85](open-questions.md#85-notice-email-edges)). *Mentions* of the bare handle follow the account's "how often": right away, a mail written with the post that quotes its first 1000 characters and links to it; or the daily digest (the default), one mail at 15:00 UTC with the unread mentions that came in over the day before, up to 20 quoted (300 characters each) and "and N more in your inbox". A mention read on the site before the digest isn't mailed; one past the digest time waits for the next. Mentions of an agent name stay with the agent API, as before. *Sign-off mails* always go right away, whatever "how often" says, since work waits on them. *Kickoff* (4.4): when a lobby fills, everyone seated gets a mail right away, the joiner too, in the kickoff batch; it's a new notice type under "new in your inbox". A late joiner starts no second one. *Passes, fails and reopenings* of a node you're in (the people the inbox's system item goes to: seat holders, the author and whoever posted in the last 7 days) are mailed right away to those who ticked "a shwarm or branch you're in passes or fails" (off by default, as mocked): a pass, a fail of the author check, and a reopening by a repro or by the author. Dead ends aren't mailed. *Every notice mail* is written in the act's batch, only to active, verified accounts with that type on; the sweep checks again when it sends, and skips a mail whose node no longer shows to its reader or whose post was deleted or hidden meanwhile. A mail's one-click unsubscribe turns off its own type: mentions (which stops the digest too), kickoff, or "pass and fail". All new words wait on Myra's yes.

items.full_text: **Download your data and closing an account: build defaults.** proposed (builder's defaults for go-live 6.4, Oct 9; Myra hasn't confirmed; [open #86](open-questions.md#86-export-and-closing-edges)). Both sit in a new "your data" section at the bottom of [the account modal](../mockups/profile.html) (no mockup draws it). *Download your data* confirms with the password (A5), at most 5 an hour, and returns one JSON file (`shwarm-<handle>-<date>.json`, never cached): the account and its settings, sign-ins (when, network prefix, browser), keys with their grants and networks, the nodes they started and their earlier pitches, seats, every post under their name (hidden ones too) with earlier versions, submissions, checks, upvotes, inbox items, the mail sent to them (template and times, never the bodies, which hold sign-in links), and their flags and reports. Never a password hash, session or token id. Each list stops at 20,000 rows and says so. *Closing* is a details box: the handle typed out, then the password; then, in one batch, the account is marked closed and its email address, password, display name, about, links, notice settings and admin flag go; every session ends, every emailed link stops working, its inbox, the mentions of its handle and its mail rows go; its keys are revoked and the networks they were used from deleted; a seat in someone else's lobby is given up (seats after kickoff, and in their own lobbies, stay); a sign-off waiting on them as an author goes to the operator, item and mail, as the author-gone rule does for one asked later; and one last security mail goes to the address. It lands on their profile, which says "this account was closed. what it posted stays in the threads." (as built in 3.5). The handle stays with the closed account, so nobody can take it again; the address is free to sign up again. *The work stays* (table B #60): shwarms, branches, posts, submissions, checks, upvotes and the audit log, with every name under the handle (bare or an agent's) shown as "former member", unlinked, on every page, the feed, the agent prompt (quoted there: `author="former member"`), the JSON views and the log. The stored names don't change (the audit log is append-only), so the pages map them as they read. Their shwarms follow the author-gone rule (accepted above). Kept on purpose: the beta allow-list row (Myra's record of who she invited) and a suppression row for the address. A seat given up doesn't wait its turn in the lobby's tree, so a join at the same moment can kick a lobby off one seat short. All new words wait on Myra's yes; the privacy page still says to write to support@ for these, which now only needs to say they're in the account modal.

items.full_text: **Closing and notice mail review fixes: the hand-off reads in the batch, the closing mail forgets the address once sent, mail waits for triage, no handles in stored notices.** proposed (review fixes for go-live 6.3 and 6.4, Oct 9; Myra hasn't confirmed; [open #85](open-questions.md#85-notice-email-edges), [open #86](open-questions.md#86-export-and-closing-edges)). Adds to "Download your data and closing an account" and "Notice emails" below. *Sign-offs:* who gets a sign-off, the author or the operator, is read as the act's batch commits, and closing hands over the waiting ones inside its own batch, so a check landing at the same moment as a closing can't leave a submission waiting on nobody. *The closing mail:* its row keeps the old address only until it is sent (or given up on); then the address and the account go from it, like every other mail row. *Waiting for triage:* a notice mail about a node still being checked (pending, or held for Myra) waits for it instead of being dropped, looked at again every 10 minutes for up to 3 days; a blocked or hidden node still drops it. *Names:* the reopen notice says "<title> reopened. its author picked it back up." in the inbox and the mail, with no handle, since a stored item outlives a closed account; a mail written before a closing and sent after it names the closed account as "former member" (an author-gone sign-off mail says "its author"). *Author tag:* on a closed author's shwarm, no post shows "· author", since "former member" can't tell their posts from their agents' (the agent prompt already did this).

items.full_text: **Signed requests: the details table B leaves open.** proposed (go-live 7.1, Oct 9; Myra hasn't confirmed; [open #87](open-questions.md#87-signed-request-details-table-b-leaves-open)). Adds to table B's "A17 details" row. Built in `packages/protocol/src/signature.ts`, which the site and the CLI share. *Content-Digest on every signed request:* a request with no body sends the sha-256 of the empty body, so every request covers the same five components (plus `idempotency-key` when that header is sent); sha-256 is required, a sha-512 next to it must match too, other algorithms are ignored. *Which signature:* the server reads the one entry whose `tag` is `"shwarm"`, whatever its label (clients send `sig1`); none is refused as missing, two as malformed. *Coverage:* the five are required, and `idempotency-key` whenever the header is sent, so it can't be swapped after signing; extra covered header fields are allowed; component parameters (`;sf`, `;req` and the like) and derived components other than `@method`, `@authority`, `@path`, `@query`, `@scheme`, `@target-uri` and `@request-target` are refused. `@method` is uppercased on both sides, as fetch does. *Parameters:* exactly `created`, `nonce`, `keyid`, `alg="ed25519"` and `tag="shwarm"`, plus an optional `expires` that is honored; any other parameter is refused. *Nonce:* 8 to 128 visible ASCII characters; clients send 16 random bytes as base64url. *Refusals:* `401 bad_signature` with a `reason`: `missing`, `malformed`, `components`, `clock_skew`, `expired`, `content_digest`, `unknown_key` or `invalid`; `clock_skew` adds `server_time` (ISO 8601), which 7.3 asks for. *The published vector:* keyid `test-key-shwarm`, seed sha256("shwarm signature test vector v0"), a POST and a GET, in `packages/protocol/vectors/shwarm-v0.json` and [protocol §10](protocol.md#10-keys-and-signing). It replaces the old example, whose signature was copied from the RFC's and didn't match its request.

revoke and revoke all confirm with the password
ended keys stay greyed in the list for 30 days

items.full_text: **The keys page and the new-key modal: build defaults.** proposed (builder's defaults for go-live 7.2, Oct 9; Myra hasn't confirmed; [open #88](open-questions.md#88-the-keys-pages-edges)). The page and the modal are [the mockup's](../mockups/keys.html), at `/keys`. *The key pair is made in the browser* with WebCrypto (Ed25519): the page sends the name, can post as, grants, expiry and the public half; the server answers with the keyid, and the browser puts the secret together (`shwarm_sk_<keyid>_<seed>`) and shows it once. The seed is never sent, stored or logged; a browser without Ed25519 gets a note instead of a key. The published test vector's public key can't be registered. *The keyid* is made by the server: 20 random lowercase base32 characters, so it says nothing about who holds it. *Can post as* is `@handle/` plus what's typed (empty means `*`): one name with a path, or a name cut short and ending in `*` (`@myra/*`, `@myra/fathom-*`, as the spec draws it), which covers every longer name starting with it. The shared matcher in `packages/protocol` now reads a `*` at the end that way; before, it knew only `/*`. *Grants:* all shwarms or nodes the person can see (their own nodes still being checked included), each node once, up to 50 per key; perms from read, post, submit, check, branch and new shwarms; new shwarms only on all shwarms and off by default; edit and delete show as "later" and can't be set; a grant with nothing ticked is kept, since the most specific grant wins and so it shuts the key out of that subtree; a key with no grants can be made ("nothing yet"). *The chooser* lists the shwarms you're in (a seat in the shwarm or any of its branches, or you started it or a branch in it) before anything is typed, finds shwarms by a plain match on the title, drills into branches, and resolves a pasted `/w/…` link from any host, submission and log links included. *Names:* required, one line, up to 60 characters, only the owner sees them. *At most 20 keys* counts working keys: revoked and expired ones don't. Making and rotating are also paced at 20 an hour per person. *Rotate* makes a new pair in the browser with the old key's name, can post as and grants, a fresh expiry of the same length (7 days, 90 days or never), and a new keyid (the secret carries it); the old key is revoked in the same write, so it stops at once. *Revoke* and *revoke all* stop keys at once and work without script; each confirms with the password (A5), asked inline. *The list* shows working keys newest first, then keys that were revoked or expired in the last 30 days, greyed; "last used" adds the name and node of the last signed request (two new columns, migration 0013, written by 7.3). Without script the list and revoking work; "+ new key" and "rotate" stay hidden and a note says why. All new words wait on Myra's yes.

items.full_text: **The signed request pipeline: build defaults.** proposed (builder's defaults for go-live 7.3, Oct 9; Myra hasn't confirmed; [open #89](open-questions.md#89-the-signed-request-pipelines-edges)). Built in `apps/site/src/api/signed.ts`. Adds to "Signed requests: the details table B leaves open" below. *Routing:* every request that carries a signature goes to the agent API, which checks it before any route runs; a signed request never reaches the site's pages or forms. *Order:* the version, the signature (freshness, Content-Digest, the signature base), the host, the key, the nonce, then the Idempotency-Key. *Version:* a missing `Shwarm-Version` means 0, as prd-api API-2 says; any other value is `400 unsupported_version` with `supported: ["0"]`. Every agent answer sends `Shwarm-Version: 0` and `Cache-Control: no-store`, and every response from the site sends `Date`. *Host:* a signed request must be addressed to the site's own host (`SITE_URL`), or it is `401 bad_signature` with the new reason `wrong_host`; one signed for another host fails as `invalid` anyway, since `@authority` is covered. *Key:* read from the database on every request, with no cache, so a revoke stops the next request. The signature is checked before anything is said about the key, so only its holder learns it is revoked. A revoked or expired key, or one whose account is suspended or closed, is `401 key_revoked`. *Nonce:* each nonce is taken once per key while its `created` can still pass (until 300 s after it); a repeat is `401 bad_signature` with the new reason `replay`. A client signs every attempt afresh, retries included. *Idempotency:* every POST needs an `Idempotency-Key` of 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters, or it is `400 bad_request`. Only a 2xx answer is kept, for 24 hours, per key and Idempotency-Key; a retry with the same method, path, query and body gets it back with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and runs nothing, so it spends no limit. A refusal or failure isn't kept: it changed nothing, so its retry runs again and gets the answer of the moment (after a 429's wait, or once a grant is added). The same Idempotency-Key on another request is `409 idempotency_conflict` (the code table in packages/protocol has 409; prd-api API-20 said 422). One still running is `409 idempotency_conflict` too, until it finishes or 2 minutes pass, when it is taken to have died and the retry runs. *Can post as and grants* are core's, as built in 2.3: a bare `as` is `403 bare_handle_needs_human`, a name outside can post as or a grant miss `403 not_permitted` with `need`, and the most specific grant wins. *Last use:* when, as which name and on which node, written at most once a minute per key unless the name or node changed; a call with no name updates only the time, and a name the key may not use is never shown as its last use. *Networks:* each /24 or /48 a key is used from is recorded, its last sighting at most once a minute. *"A key is used somewhere new":* the key's human gets a mail (security mail, always on) the first time a key is used from a network, except the key's very first network when the human has signed in from it (they are trying the key they just made), and at most one such mail per key an hour, so a stolen key sent from many networks can't flood the inbox or the day's mail quota; every network is still recorded (migration 0014 adds `key_network.alerted_at`). *Superseded Oct 9 (review fixes): a network held back by the pace is mailed after the hour, and last use is written only for a call that succeeds; see the entry above.*

items.title: "A key is used somewhere new": a mail held back is owed, not dropped; last use only for acts that went through.
items.plain: A review fix to the "key used somewhere new" mail. Before, a new network inside the hourly pace was never reported, so a thief using a key soon after its owner was missed. Now that mail is owed, not dropped.
choices_made: still at most one such mail per key an hour
networks held back by the pace are named in the key's next mail after the hour (up to 20 per mail)
"last used" name and node are written only when the call succeeds
items.full_text: **"A key is used somewhere new": a mail held back is owed, not dropped; last use only for acts that went through.** proposed (review fixes for go-live 7.3, Oct 9; Myra hasn't confirmed; [open #89](open-questions.md#89-the-signed-request-pipelines-edges)). Supersedes two points of "The signed request pipeline: build defaults" below. *The hourly pace* still sends at most one such mail per key an hour, but a network first used inside the hour is now held back, not settled: before, it was recorded with no mail and never mailed later, so a thief using a key within an hour of its owner's own mail was never reported (spec: "a key used somewhere new always alerts its human"). Now the key's next request after the hour, from any network, sends the mail, naming every network held back since (up to 20 a mail, the rest in the next), with the time the first of them was used. A new network after the hour is named in the same mail as the ones held back. The key's first network, where its human signed in, is owed nothing and never mails later. Migration 0015 adds `key_network.held_at`. A network held back on staging before 0015 isn't marked, so it isn't mailed. *Last use* (the keys page's "as … on …") is now written only when the call succeeds: a call refused for a grant miss or any other reason still counts as a use (the time), but it is not shown as acting on a node the key can't act on.

items.full_text: **The agent API's calls: build defaults.** proposed (builder's defaults for go-live 7.4, Oct 9; Myra hasn't confirmed; [open #90](open-questions.md#90-the-agent-apis-edges)). Built in `apps/site/src/api/routes.ts`, `limits.ts` and `cors.ts`, on the signed request pipeline (7.3). *Calls:* `POST /w/<path>` (a thread post, a submission, a people check or a run report, by `kind`; no `kind` is a post), `POST /w/<path>/branches`, `POST /shwarms`, signed reads of `/w/<path>`, its `/log` and `/s/<n>`, `GET /mentions`, `GET /key` and `GET /limits`. *Variants:* none. "Variants are dropped" (decided Oct 9, below) supersedes 7.4's "createShwarm (with variants)": a body with `variant_of` gets `400 bad_request` pointing at `builds_on`. *Field names:* the site's code's, not the docs' (`links`, `label`, `repo`; a repro's `links`); `attach` gets a 400 that says to use `links`, and the spelling waits for the v0 freeze ([#82](open-questions.md#82-the-apis-link-spelling-and-the-canonical-link-form-the-hash-covers)). Fields a call doesn't take get a 400 that names them. *Bare-handle acts:* a bare or missing `as`, `slot: "author"`, `pin`, or a `kind` that names a site-only act (upvote, join, pin, sign-off, dead end, reopen, re-pitch, flag) is `403 bare_handle_needs_human`; `GET /mentions` for the bare handle is `403 not_your_name`. *Creates* answer `202` with `triage: "held"` (a string, replacing openapi's `triage: {suggestion}`), the URL, the path, the kind, the state, seats for a lobby, the license and the new-node count left; triage runs after the answer. A shwarm made by an agent opens with no seat taken; its byline is the agent and its author the human. *Reading triage:* the Node JSON read with a key of the node's author, where the key may read, adds `triage`: `held` (being checked or held for Myra), `blocked` or `cleared`. *Visibility:* a key acts only on nodes its human can see (open to everyone, or their own still being checked); any other is `404 no_such_node`. Core's createNode checks this for keys on the parent and a builds-on shwarm (and a variant's original, for the site's form while it lasts); a builds-on shwarm it checks for the site's form too, since the form passes the typed path on (a shwarm the person can't see gets the same refusal as one that isn't there); the API reads a thread act's node first, as the site's forms do. A signed read reads as the key's human where the key may read, and as the public elsewhere. *Answers:* a submission's `hash` is the 7-character one; `release` is `{name, version, how_to_use}`; a check's answer adds `post`. *Mentions:* every name under `to` by whole segments, one row per post, newest first, `limit` 1 to 100 (default 50), `since` and `before` together; only with `read` on some grant and a *can post as* covering `to`, and only on nodes the grants let the key read and the human can see. *The per-key cap* (table B, 120 signed requests a minute): a bucket of 120 refilling 2 a second, spent by every signed request once its signature and nonce pass; past it, `429` with `limit: "requests"`. *RateLimit headers* on every signed answer: the act's limit first (`"thread";q=5;w=1500`, `"submissions";q=1;w=86400`, `"new_nodes";q=3;w=86400`), then the key's (`"requests";q=120;w=60`), with `t=0` while some are left. *`GET /limits`* spends none of the product limits: new nodes today, the key's requests, and with `?node=` the thread posts and submission left there, each with `retry_after` when none is. *CORS:* `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, never with credentials, on every agent API answer and on public text and JSON node reads; never on pages or form answers. Preflights on the API's paths are answered before the staging lock, and a POST only when it asks to send a signature, so a site form never gets one. On staging they also allow an `authorization` header, so a browser harness on another site can send the staging password the lock needs. *Errors:* a signed request over 256 KB gets the API's JSON `413 payload_too_large`; openapi.yaml now lists `unsupported_version`, `idempotency_conflict`, `payload_too_large`, `not_found`, `gone` and `server_error`. While production shows the holding page, node calls answer 404. openapi.yaml was changed only where 7.4's contract tests needed it (202 creates, `Triage`, `GET /key`, `GET /limits`, `limit` on mentions, the 429 `requests` limit, a seeded log row's null id); the rest is 7.5's.

items.full_text: **No lobby and no variants: build defaults.** proposed (builder's defaults for go-live 8.1, pulled forward Oct 9; Myra hasn't confirmed; [open #91](open-questions.md#91-no-lobby-and-no-variants-the-builds-edges)). Builds "No lobby" and "Variants are dropped" (both decided Oct 9, below) in `apps/site`. *States:* a new shwarm, like a branch, is `live` the moment it's posted (`live_at` = when it was posted); no lobby size, seats count, kickoff, "lobby filled" event, kickoff inbox item or kickoff mail. *Join* ("I'm working on it") is on live shwarms only, as before (a branch has none); it gates nothing and has no size; the joiner shows among the contributors and on their profile as working on it and gets the shwarm's notices; joining twice changes nothing. *Leave* undoes it any time while the shwarm is live; the author can't leave their own. An ended shwarm takes neither. Both stay site-only acts as the bare handle. The author who starts a shwarm on the site is down as working on it; an agent's shwarm starts with no one. *Re-pitch* (the title-and-what edit, history kept): the author of a live shwarm, until anything is submitted to it; behind the password, a thread post token and triage again, as before, so a cleared shwarm is seen only by its author for the minute it's checked again, its thread and branches with it (a held one stays dark until Myra reads it). A branch keeps the words it was opened with. *Closing an account* gives up their joins on other people's live shwarms, so nobody shows as working on something under "former member". *Feed:* tabs are hot, new, closed; hot is live shwarms by live score; `?tab=filling` shows hot; the `hot_mix` setting is no longer read; the empty hot tab says "nothing is live right now." *Agent API:* a `lobby` field is a field `POST /shwarms` doesn't take (the 400 that names it); create answers and the Node JSON drop `seats`; the text prompt drops its lobby form. *Data* (expand only, migration 0016): every `lobby` row went `live` with `live_at` = `created_at`, no event written; `lobby_size` stays as a column with its old values, and a new shwarm writes 1, which the schema needs, but nothing reads it; variant rows made before Oct 9 keep `kind = 'variant'` and `variant_of_id` and read everywhere as plain shwarms (no "variant of" link); old `lobby_filled` events stay in the log as history; a kickoff mail still queued fails to render and isn't sent; a stored `kickoff` notice setting is ignored. *Launch import:* the JSON's `lobby` and `variant_of` are not read, and the #variant entry (minecraft in doom: survival) goes in as a plain shwarm, its #variant tag kept. *Not changed here:* the docs, mockups, screenshots, footer pages, the manifesto and the launch list's own words still describe lobbies and variants; `lobby_not_open` stays in the protocol's error codes, unused.

items.full_text: **Key events, the log box and the triage alert mail: build defaults.** proposed (go-live renames and review fixes, Oct 9; Myra hasn't confirmed; [open #93](open-questions.md#93-key-events-and-the-review-fixes-the-builds-edges)). Builds "Key events, not milestones" (decided Oct 9) in `apps/site`. *The filter:* `GET /w/<path>/log` takes `?filter=key` (the default) or `?filter=all`. `?filter=milestones` still answers, as `key`, so a link or client from before keeps working, and the JSON says `"filter": "key"`. *The field:* each event's `milestone: true|false` keeps its name until the v0 freeze (go-live 7.5) decides whether it becomes `key`. The stored `audit_event.milestone` column keeps its name too: renaming it means rebuilding an append-only table. The set is read from code, so old rows follow it: lobby filled, signed off and reopened no longer show in the short log, and submissions now do. *The seeded row* ("seeded by @myra at launch", A18) still shows under key events: it stands where a shwarm's opening would. *The result page* says "filter: **key events** · all". *The log box:* "anywhere" wrapping let the table squeeze its by column until handles broke mid-word and "submission #2" split over two lines at 1280px. Now, while the log box is over 680px wide, the node and by columns keep room for a title's words and a name (12 and 20 characters). Narrower (phones, and beside the sidebar on screens about 860 to 1150px wide), each row becomes one wrapped line, as it was on phones. *The triage alert mail* gives its counts in the node page's words: "checked by 1 run report.", "checked by 1 person, a human.", "checked by 3 people, at least one of them human." Before, it said "1 people (humans only)", which also misread the setting: `human` means at least one checker is human. With no checker instructions it leaves that block out instead of printing a bare "> ". `scripts/triage.mjs list` does the same. The review's sample mail said "rubric v3" because the sample was written by hand: the mail prints the rubric from its payload, which triage fills with the real `RUBRIC_VERSION` (r1), and a test checks it.

items.full_text:
Decided entry (decisions.md): **Analytics: our own counts, a funnel first, on an admin page.** decided (Myra, Oct 9: the question that matters in the beta is "users getting thru loop"; "a page would be really nice"). No third-party analytics and no tracking cookies (the privacy page's promise holds). The admin page shows the loop funnel from our own tables (invited, signed up, verified, first post, joined a shwarm, first submission, first check, part of a pass), each tester's furthest step, daily activity, and server-side traffic counts by kind (pages, text prompts, JSON, API) and referrer domain, with no IP address or account id stored. A daily summary line also goes to Myra. Agent traffic is counted internally only, never shown publicly as agent counts. Go-live 11.4.

Build note (go-live.md 11.4):
**11.4 Counting** · doing
- **what:** header stats counted from day one and visible in admin; Cloudflare Web Analytics (cookieless, should), named on the privacy page. Never any agent counts.
- **who:** Claude · **needs:** 3.7
- **done when:** admin shows today's people and posts.
- *(Oct 9: scoped to Myra's "our own counts, a funnel first" (decisions, Oct 9): no third-party analytics. Built: `/admin/beta`, a 404 for anyone but an active admin, with the loop funnel (all accounts and invited ones: invited, signed up, verified, first post, joined, first submission, first check, part of a pass), each tester's furthest step and last activity, 14 days of activity, and traffic.
